<description>
A few of our longer-running tests have some unnecessary waits and timeouts in them. Reduce or replace them to shorten test times:

- in `p2p_node_network_limited` replace the expected sync timeout with header/ping barriers and a bounded negative check. At CI timeout factor 40, saves roughly 195 seconds per transport.
- in `interface_ipc_mining` cap three expected no-event waits at five seconds, saving roughly 105 seconds at factor 40 in CI.
- in `WalletLoadingDescriptors` honor sanity mode’s single epoch, avoiding four unnecessary wallet unload/load cycles.
- two wallet unit tests switch to `BasicTestingSetup` avoiding construction of two unused 100-block chains.

The timeout changes alone save approximately eight minutes of accumulated test-worker time on CI jobs running both transports and IPC mining. Wall-clock savings depend on parallel scheduling, CPU etc.
</description>

<commits>
06cb869112 test: shorten network limited negative wait

CI scaled a negative sync timeout to 200 seconds per transport. The test
now waits for header sync and a ping roundtrip, then checks that the IBD
node sends no block requests for up to five seconds.

79bb94f092 test: cap expected IPC timeouts

Expected no-event checks can otherwise each wait for the full timeout
factor, which reaches 40 seconds on CI. Cap those checks at five
seconds while keeping readiness waits on the normal scaled timeout.

40619d0687 bench: honor configured wallet epochs

The benchmark sanity runner selects one epoch, but the benchmark
unconditionally replaced that setting with five. Cap the configured
epoch count at five so sanity runs remain short.

ce1d88b263 test: avoid unused wallet test chains

These tests do not use chain state, but their fixtures mine 100 blocks
before each case. BasicTestingSetup provides the node context without
the unnecessary chain construction.
</commits>
